phase3_findings.description: No test appends while the widget is closed after it has been opened; the Chatbot stays mounted but hidden, so the append goes through controller.addMessages, and a change routing on isOpen instead of on a mounted Chatbot would silently lose those appends with every test still passing.

The two guards on staging a failed turn's attachments again are untested: the composer not being refilled (refilled false) and the user staging new files during the failed turn (stagedAttachments.length === 0).
No test reaches the History-switch branch for a data source with listConversations but no getConversation, which also clears appendedRef.

The mount test never confirms the appendBlocks call was queued (a pending timer) before unmount(), so a synchronously attached handle would let it pass without exercising the if (unmounted) return guard in flush.

README line 120 says the typed text goes back into the empty input when sendMessage rejects, but a typed slash command whose run calls ctx.send is not refilled: sendTurn(text, { echo: true }) at ChatController.ts 295 passes no typed, so onTurnFailed never runs (the test 'does not report text a command sent as a failed turn' pins this).

The ControllerHost.onTurnFailed TSDoc says returning true means the attachments are staged again, but the code restages them only when the user has not staged new ones (line 420, this.stagedAttachments.length === 0).
Added test comments in ChatWidget.test.tsx (lines 73-75, 80, 81, 105-106, 109) are worked arithmetic or background about mobile viewports rather than reasons.

appendBlocks adds an empty avatar row with no console output when a block has a string type nothing renders (a typo against a registered custom type, a missing blockRenderers entry, or a table without headers/rows): answerToMessages keeps it, BlockRenderer returns null (BlockRenderer.tsx 110-111), and no warning fires, so a host's dropped card gives no signal.

A ChatWidgetHandle kept after the React widget unmounts drops appendBlocks calls silently: mountedResetKeyRef keeps its last value (the layout effect at 498-500 has no cleanup), so the call goes to controller.addMessages, which calls the unmounted kit's setState and never checks disposed (ChatController.ts 201-208); the mount() wrapper warns for the same misuse.

The SendMessageResponse.blocks TSDoc says any other answer that shows nothing gets an apology, but an answer whose only block has a type with no renderer, or a malformed built-in block, shows nothing and gets no apology (messages.length > 0 at ChatController.ts 397-401).

A silent turn (blocks: [] with no sources) ends with no reply and no console line, so a backend returning an empty array on an internal failure looks like an ignored question with no trace for the developer; documented behavior, a diagnostic gap.

When ChatWidget throws during its first render, ref.current stays null and mount()'s flush reschedules every 10 ms indefinitely while later handle calls, appendBlocks included, pile up in queued with no warning.

README line 120 says a failed turn's typed text always goes back into the empty input, which does not happen for a typed slash command whose run calls ctx.send (sendTurn(text, { echo: true }) at ChatController.ts 295 never passes typed).

AttachmentPicker.tsx line 90 still says the listener clears chips when the controller takes the attachments, but the listener now also restores a failed turn's attachments (ChatController.ts 420-423); the matching onAttachmentsReset TSDoc was updated, this comment was not.

No test checks that mount()'s appendBlocks reaches the widget, either replayed from the queue or forwarded after the ref attaches; mount.test.tsx covers only the after-unmount path, so wiring it to the wrong method would pass every test.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no Critical findings; 2 Important findings and 13 Suggestion items sit below the critical threshold; 4 checklist items inconclusive)

The PR can merge: no finding or checklist failure reaches the configured critical threshold, and every fix from the earlier rounds is in place at this head, though two Important silent-drop gaps in `appendBlocks` are worth a look.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and inconclusive checklist items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` lines 508-520: `appendBlocks` adds an empty avatar row with no console output when a block has a string `type` that nothing renders, such as a typo like `raddy_card` for a registered `raddy-card`, a missing `blockRenderers` entry, or `{ type: 'table' }` without `headers` or `rows`. The blank-text and typeless-block warnings do not catch this case, `answerToMessages` (`src/chat/ChatController.ts` 148-155) keeps the block, and `BlockRenderer` returns `null` for it (`src/blocks/BlockRenderer.tsx` 110-111). This is the main path for host cards, so the host gets no signal when a card is dropped. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` line 519, with `src/chat/ChatController.ts` lines 201-208: a `ChatWidgetHandle` kept after the React widget unmounts drops `appendBlocks` calls without a warning. `mountedResetKeyRef` keeps its last value because the layout effect at 498-500 has no cleanup, so the call goes to `controller.addMessages`, which calls the unmounted kit's `setState` and never checks `disposed`. The `mount()` wrapper warns for the same misuse (`src/mount.tsx` 36-38), so the two embeddings report it differently. (raised by 1/5 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (13)

<details><summary>13 items</summary>

1. `README.md` line 120 says that when `sendMessage` rejects and the input is empty, "the text the user typed goes back into it". This is false for a typed slash command whose `run` calls `ctx.send(...)`: `sendTurn(text, { echo: true })` at `src/chat/ChatController.ts` 295 passes no `typed`, so `onTurnFailed` never runs, and the test "does not report text a command sent as a failed turn" (`src/chat/ChatController.test.ts` 233-248) pins that behavior. (raised by 2/5 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: mechanism under discussion is ChatController.performTurn's onTurnFailed refill, which runs only for typed turns; scoping the README sentence changes no output, branch or covered set; grep of the head view for "goes back into it" printed only README.md:120, and the only file naming README is package.json line 31 (the npm "files" list, a publishing list, not a behavior reader); README is published, so limb two fails and the cap is Important, weighed at the original Suggestion -->
2. `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` lines 498-520: no test appends while the widget is closed after it has been opened. After the first open the Chatbot stays mounted but hidden, so the append goes through `controller.addMessages`; a change that routed on `isOpen` instead of on whether a Chatbot is mounted would lose those appends and every current test would still pass. (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. `src/chat/ChatController.ts` lines 418-423: the two guards on staging a failed turn's attachments again are untested, namely the composer not being refilled and the user staging new files during the failed turn. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` lines 376-381: no test reaches the History-switch branch for a data source with `listConversations` but no `getConversation`, which also clears `appendedRef`. (raised by 1/5 agents)
5. `src/mount.test.tsx` lines 15-19: the mount test never confirms the call was queued (a pending timer) before `unmount()`, so a handle that attached synchronously would make the test pass without exercising the `if (unmounted) return` guard. (raised by 1/5 agents)
6. `src/mount.tsx` line 63: no test checks that `mount()`'s `appendBlocks` reaches the widget, either replayed from the queue or forwarded after the ref attaches; wiring it to the wrong method would pass every test. This is the entry point for non-React hosts, including the standalone build. (raised by 1/5 agents)
7. `src/chat/ChatController.ts` lines 77-80: the `ControllerHost.onTurnFailed` TSDoc says returning true means "its attachments are staged again", but the code stages them again only when the user has not staged new ones (line 420, `this.stagedAttachments.length === 0`). 8. `src/types.ts` lines 113-114: the `SendMessageResponse.blocks` TSDoc says any other answer that shows nothing gets an apology, but an answer whose only block has a type with no renderer, or a malformed built-in block, shows nothing and gets no apology (`messages.length > 0` at `src/chat/ChatController.ts` 397-401; the renderer returns `null`). The behavior is documented. (raised by 1/5 agents)
11. `src/mount.tsx` lines 45-53: when `ChatWidget` throws during its first render, `ref.current` stays null and `flush` reschedules itself every 10 ms indefinitely, while later handle calls pile up in `queued` with no warning. (raised by 1/5 agents)

- VC-8: FAIL (suggestion) — The SendMessageResponse.blocks TSDoc asserts that every answer other than an empty blocks array with no sources that shows nothing (only blank text, blocks without a type, or sources without a title) gets an apology. [src/types.ts:110]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  types.ts:110-115 says any other answer that shows nothing gets an apology. Counterexample: sendMessage returns { blocks: [{ type: 'unknown-x' }] } with no matching blockRenderers. answerToMessages (ChatController.ts:136-155) keeps the block, since its type is a string. isPlainText is false, so it returns one non-empty BLOCKS_MESSAGE. performTurn (ChatController.ts:393-401) then sees messages.length > 0 and shows no apology. BlockRenderer.tsx:110-111 returns null for a type with no custom renderer (the file header says it is 'ignored when no renderer exists'). The user sees an empty blocks container and no apology. The same happens for a block with an unknown type plus an empty-text labelled block. So the absolute claim is false, and the TSDoc over-promises. The text only lists blank text, typeless blocks and untitled sources, and omits unrendered unknown types.

  </details>
